messages.subject: Binomial data[0] (nb,y) = (1,2695.76) is void
parts:
Dear all INLA experts,

I am working on a project about population distribution. Y variable is population abundance. I built an INLA model as following:

#defining the model formula and model type
form <-  gr ~ 0 + b0 +  season + year + f(s, model=spde) 

#this is where the model is run
rl.nb2.gr <- inla(form, family='binomial', 
                  data=inla.stack.data(stke), 
                  control.compute=list(dic=TRUE), 
                  control.inla=list(int.strategy="eb"), 
                  control.predictor=list(A=inla.stack.A(stke)),
                  control.fixed = list(expand.factor.strategy='inla'), 
                  verbose=FALSE)

But I got an error message: 
*** ERROR ***   INLA.Data1: Binomial data[0] (nb,y) = (1,2695.76) is void
Error in inla.inlaprogram.has.crashed() : 
  The inla-program exited with an error. Unless you interupted it yourself, please rerun with verbose=TRUE and check the output carefully.
  If this does help; please contact the developers at <he...@r-inla.org>.
In addition: Warning message:
running command '"C:\Users\ADMINI~1\AppData\Local\Temp\RtmpAxkHfB\file477c1c50360d.BAT"' had status 1 

When I changed the Y variable to persistence (0 or 1), the model worked.

Is there any idea to fix this?

Thanks,
Ruby

Hi,

the problem is that its an error in the input, for a binomial(n,p),
your n=1 but the response is 2695.76,  which is void. so something is
wrong in the input.
